newsitem.title: CHINA: Ex-Merrill Lynch banker Wallace charged in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Merrill Lynch banker Wallace charged in Hong Kong.

text.p: Hong Kong police on Wednesday charged a former top Merrill Lynch and Co Inc banker with money laundering, following an inquiry sparked by fraud allegations.
Kevin Wallace, a 46-year-old American who was detained in Hong Kong on July 7, was due to appear in court later in the day, police said.
Wallace was seized by the Commercial Crime Bureau 10 days ago along with an unidentified Chinese man in connection with an alleged fraud said to involve up to US$30 million.
The formal charge against him was "dealing with the proceeds of an indictable offence" under article 25 of Hong Kong's Organised and Serious Crimes Ordinance, a police spokesman said.
A former private banking star at Merrill Lynch International Bank Ltd, Singapore, Wallace posted bail of more than HK$1 million on July 9.
The charge was laid after Wallace reported to police on Wednesday morning, a condition of his bail.
Merrill Lynch started civil proceedings against Wallace last month in Singapore and Hong Kong, and the company has filed a criminal complaint in Singapore.
The U.S. investment bank accused Wallace of engaging in "unauthorised trading, misrepresenting or falsifying private clients' statements and forging client signatures".
In his job at Merrill Lynch, Wallace acted as a financial consultant to wealthy clients across Asia, taking investment orders and providing advice.
Industry sources said his clients were believed to have bank balances ranging from a few million to US$25 million.
Wallace was employed by Merrill Lynch from late 1991 until he was dismissed on May 15 this year.
Merrill Lynch has not commented on the amount in question in the case, but industry sources and media reports have put it at around US$30 million.
Merrill Lynch has said that the costs it might incur from the alleged fraud would not be "significant to Merrill Lynch's business or financial position".
The company made US$1.6 billion profit last year.
Merrill spokesman Robert Grieves said earlier the investment bank had settled with about half of Wallace's clients.
